title: A room with no floor, read from above: a man and a board on any face of the Wreck, the pop-up, the hatches and the trunk
about: v0.0.25, "Hold to hold", takes the shoot house's drill aboard the Wreck at Phobos: two decks of a stripped hull at micro-g on mag boots, where you go head first down a trunk into the hold and plant your boots on its deckhead, and a target can stand out of any of six faces. The stage draws from 45° above, so a thing 2.2 m up on the deckhead is drawn 35 px up the screen, over the floor north of it. Every figure here is the game's own (the shoot house's marine in the black combat EVA suit; the khaki turner boards), turned by the face it stands on: the deck upright, the deckhead and the dorsal (north) bulkhead flipped top to bottom, the ventral (south) bulkhead upright, starboard and port a quarter turn with the feet to the face; the deck is void-look's plate at 16 px/m, snapped to the stage's palette. K (K-a, your star of 2026-11-20 and the game's; v0.0.25's default was K-b) is how a thing on the deckhead reads: the hold with the marine on all six faces and the trunk's two scuttles, beside it a slice of the brig with a board on a cell's deckhead drawn over the passage (the case that reads wrong), and the deckhead man three times larger; K-a the projection alone (the float pick's shadow under each body off the deck), K-b and the overhead's footprint dashed on the deck below everything on the deckhead, K-c and your compartment's deckhead edge, K-d drawn at its plan spot, flipped and dotted (VIEWS §3.5's own sentence: it would also change how v0.0.24 draws a floating body's height). T (T-a) a board on each face, turned out of it or foreshortened by its tilt; P (P-b, your star and the game's) the pop-up rising over 400 ms, hinged out or sliding from a slot; H (H-b, your star and the game's) the deck hatch, square with four dogs and a yellow coaming or round with a wheel; B (B-a) the bulkhead hatch, oval with dogs or square with a lever, face on and from above; X (X-a) going down a deck through the trunk: the trunk side on, then seven frames of the picture changing from deck 5 to deck 6, the stair's wipe with the camera held or a cut with the camera held on you and gliding back. K, T, P, H and B are scored (2026-11-20); X waits, the game at X-a until you score it.

groups.title: K: a thing on the deckhead, read from above
groups.about: The hold (deck 6, 9.2 × 7.2 m) with the marine on the deck, the deckhead, the dorsal bulkhead at 1.1 m, starboard, port and the ventral bulkhead at 1.4 m; the trunk's two scuttles at 4.6, 3.6 (the deck's dogged under the deckhead's open); two cargo stacks and two lamps. Beside it the brig (deck 5): a board on the deckhead of a south cell by its cut wall, drawn over the passage; your #2 in the passage; a man half out of the deck's scuttle. Then the deckhead man three times larger. The legend under the picture names each body's face.

groups.title: X: through the trunk
groups.about: X: going down a deck. The Wreck's two decks are stacked, deck 5 above and deck 6 (the hold) below, joined by the trunk: a round shaft 0.8 m wide with a hatch, a scuttle, at each end. The stage looks down on one deck at a time, so when you go through the trunk the whole picture has to change from deck 5 to deck 6. At the left the trunk side on: the two decks as two floors, the trunk between them with its two scuttles as grey rims, you in it head first, and the camera's eye 45° above the deck it shows. Then seven frames, left to right, are that change, the time over each and what it is under it. First frame: deck 5's passage from above, you at the scuttle in its floor, going in head first. Last frame: deck 6's hold from above, you hanging head down under the scuttle in its ceiling, about to plant your boots on it (the grey ring with its wheel just below you in the picture is that ceiling scuttle, H-b as the game draws it, drawn where it shows from above, so you can see where it is). X-a: deck 5 dissolves into deck 6 in a pixel wipe over 400 ms, the wipe the game uses on a stair, and you stay on the same spot of the screen. X-b: the picture cuts to deck 6 at once, shifted so you stay where you were on screen, then the camera glides back to its usual place over 600 ms. Pick the change that reads better: it decides every hatch between decks (the Wreck now, the hauler's decks next). Redrawn and re-explained for your note of 2026-11-20, "I don't know what I'm looking at, make an effort to explain what I'm looking at please."
